14: Every integer greater than 1 is a product of primes, uniquely up to the order of the factors.
15: For every prime \(p\) and integer \(a\), \(a^p\equiv a\pmod p\); if \(p\nmid a\), then \(a^{p-1}\equiv 1\pmod p\).

18: For integers \(a,b\), there exist integers \(x,y\) such that \(ax+by=\gcd(a,b)\).
19: For pairwise coprime positive integers \(m_1,\ldots,m_k\), the map \(\mathbb{Z}/(m_1\cdots m_k)\mathbb{Z}\to\prod_{i=1}^k\mathbb{Z}/m_i\mathbb{Z}\) given by reduction modulo each \(m_i\) is an isomorphism.
20: If \(a<b\) are real numbers, there is a rational number \(q\) with \(a<q<b\).
22: There are infinitely many integer triples \((x,y,z)\) of positive integers satisfying \(x^2+y^2=z^2\); in fact, there are infinitely many primitive such triples.
23: For a simple lattice polygon with \(I\) interior and \(B\) boundary lattice points, its area is \(I+\frac{B}{2}-1\).
24: Every convex polyhedron has \(V-E+F=2\), where \(V,E,F\) are its numbers of vertices, edges and faces.
25: The real numbers are uncountable; in particular, irrational real numbers exist.
26: Every nonconstant polynomial with complex coefficients has a complex root.
27: If \(f\) is continuous on \([a,b]\), then \(F(x)=\int_a^x f(t)\,dt\) is differentiable on \((a,b)\) with \(F\prime(x)=f(x)\), and \(\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=G(b)-G(a)\) for every antiderivative \(G\) of \(f\).
28: If \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous and \(f(a)\le y\le f(b)\) (or \(f(b)\le y\le f(a)\)), then \(f(c)=y\) for some \(c\in[a,b]\).
29: Every continuous real-valued function on a compact interval attains both a maximum and a minimum.
30: Every bounded sequence in \(\mathbb{R}^n\) has a convergent subsequence.
31: A subset of \(\mathbb{R}^n\) is compact if and only if it is closed and bounded.
32: If \(f\) is continuous on \([a,b]\) and differentiable on \((a,b)\), then some \(c\in(a,b)\) satisfies \(f\prime(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}\).

37: For every real \(x\), \(e^{ix}=\cos x+i\sin x\); in particular, \(e^{i\pi}+1=0\).
39: Every symmetric polynomial in \(n\) variables over a commutative ring is uniquely a polynomial in the elementary symmetric polynomials.
40: Every square matrix \(A\) over a field satisfies its characteristic polynomial: \(\chi_A(A)=0\).
41: For a linear map \(T:V\to W\) between finite-dimensional vector spaces, \(\dim V=\dim\ker(T)+\dim\operatorname{im}(T)\).
42: For finite-dimensional subspaces \(U,W\) of a vector space, \(\dim(U+W)+\dim(U\cap W)=\dim U+\dim W\).
43: Every real symmetric matrix is diagonalizable by an orthogonal matrix; equivalently, it has an orthonormal basis of real eigenvectors.
44: Every finite abelian group is a direct product of cyclic groups of prime-power order (equivalently, it has an invariant-factor decomposition).
45: If \(|G|=p^n m\) with \(p\nmid m\), then \(G\) has a subgroup of order \(p^n\); all such subgroups are conjugate, and their number is congruent to \(1\pmod p\) and divides \(m\).
46: If a prime \(p\) divides the order of a finite group \(G\), then \(G\) contains an element of order \(p\).
47: For points \(D,E,F\) on the three sides of a triangle, the cevians \(AD,BE,CF\) are concurrent exactly when the product of the three directed side ratios is \(1\) (with the standard directed-ratio convention).
48: A prime \(p\equiv 1\pmod 4\) can be written as \(p=x^2+y^2\) for integers \(x,y\).
49: For distinct odd primes \(p,q\), \(\left(\frac pq\right)\left(\frac qp\right)=(-1)^{\frac{p-1}{2}\frac{q-1}{2}}\), where \(\left(\frac{\cdot}{\cdot}\right)\) is the Legendre symbol.
50: The polynomial ring \(F[x]\) over a field \(F\) has unique factorization into irreducible polynomials, up to units and order.
51: For \(f,g\in F[x]\), there are \(u,v\in F[x]\) with \(uf+vg=d\), where \(d\) is the monic greatest common divisor of \(f\) and \(g\).
52: If \(e_k\) are the elementary symmetric polynomials and \(p_j=\sum_i x_i^j\), then \(k e_k=\sum_{i=1}^{k}(-1)^{i-1}e_{k-i}p_i\), with \(e_0=1\).
55: For \(n\ge 2\), the number of spanning trees on \(n\) labeled vertices is \(n^{n-2}\).
56: A finite family \(A_1,\ldots,A_n\) of finite sets has a system of distinct representatives if and only if every subfamily \(\mathcal{F}\) satisfies \(|\bigcup_{A\in\mathcal{F}} A|\ge |\mathcal{F}|\).
57: In every finite bipartite graph, the maximum matching size equals the minimum vertex-cover size.
58: For a closed orientable surface of genus \(g\), its Euler characteristic is \(\chi=2-2g\).
59: Every planar graph is vertex-colorable with at most five colors.
60: For iid random variables \(X_1,X_2,\ldots\) with finite variance and mean \(\mu\), the sample mean \(\overline{X}_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n X_i\) converges in probability to \(\mu\).
61: For iid random variables with mean \(\mu\) and finite positive variance \(\sigma^2\), \(\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n}X_i-n\mu}{\sigma\sqrt{n}}\) converges in distribution to the standard normal law.
62: For events \(A_n\), if \(\sum P(A_n)<\infty\) then \(P(A_n\text{ infinitely often})=0\); if the \(A_n\) are independent and \(\sum P(A_n)=\infty\), that probability is \(1\).
63: If \(\phi\) is convex and \(\lambda_i\ge 0\) with \(\sum\lambda_i=1\), then \(\phi(\sum\lambda_i x_i)\le\sum\lambda_i\phi(x_i)\).
65: In a complete metric space, every countable intersection of open dense sets is dense.
66: Every contraction of a nonempty complete metric space into itself has a unique fixed point.
67: For compact Hausdorff \(K\), a subset of \(C(K)\) is relatively compact in the uniform norm if and only if it is uniformly bounded and equicontinuous.
68: A real subalgebra of \(C(K)\), for compact Hausdorff \(K\), that contains constants and separates points is dense in \(C(K)\) in the uniform norm.
69: A bounded linear functional on a subspace of a real normed space extends to the whole space with the same norm.
70: An arbitrary product of compact topological spaces is compact in the product topology.
71: Every continuous linear functional \(L\) on a Hilbert space has the form \(L(x)=\langle x,y\rangle\) for a unique vector \(y\).
72: Every bounded surjective linear map between Banach spaces is open.
73: A linear map between Banach spaces that is defined everywhere and has a closed graph is continuous.

78: If \(f\) is holomorphic on a simply connected domain, its integral around every closed piecewise-smooth curve \(\gamma\) is zero, and \(f\) has a primitive there.
79: Every bounded entire function \(f:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}\) is constant.
80: If \(f\) is holomorphic on and inside a positively oriented simple closed contour \(\gamma\), then \(f(z)=\frac{1}{2\pi i}\oint_{\gamma}\frac{f(\zeta)}{\zeta-z}\,d\zeta\) for \(z\) inside \(\gamma\).

83: Every simple closed curve in the plane separates the plane into a bounded and an unbounded component, both having the curve as boundary.
84: For a finite Galois extension \(L/K\) with group \(G\), intermediate fields correspond bijectively, with reversed inclusion, to subgroups of \(G\) via fixed fields.
85: If \(R\) is a Noetherian ring, then the polynomial ring \(R[x]\) is Noetherian.
86: If \(A\) is a finitely generated integral domain over a field \(k\), then \(A\) is integral over a polynomial subalgebra \(k[y_1,\ldots,y_d]\) for some algebraically independent \(y_i\).
87: For an algebraically closed field \(k\) and an ideal \(I\subseteq k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\), the polynomials vanishing on its zero set form \(\sqrt{I}\).
88: Every finite separable field extension \(L/K\) is generated by one element: \(L=K(\alpha)\) for some \(\alpha\in L\).
89: A compact self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space has an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors for the closure of its range; its nonzero eigenvalues have finite multiplicity and can accumulate only at \(0\).
90: Every Boolean algebra is isomorphic to the algebra of clopen subsets of a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space.
91: Every subgroup of a free group is free.
92: Every finite integral domain is a field.
93: For a smooth manifold, de Rham cohomology is naturally isomorphic to singular cohomology with real coefficients.
94: Every closed differential form on a star-shaped open subset of \(\mathbb{R}^n\) is exact in positive degree.
95: If \(f\) and \(g\) are holomorphic inside and on a simple closed contour \(\gamma\) and \(|f-g|<|f|\) on \(\gamma\), then \(f\) and \(g\) have the same number of zeros inside \(\gamma\), counted with multiplicity.
96: The prime-counting function satisfies \(\pi(x)\sim\frac{x}{\log x}\) as \(x\to\infty\).
97: For integers \(a,m\) with \(m\ge 1\) and \(\gcd(a,m)=1\), infinitely many primes \(q\) are congruent to \(a\pmod m\).
98: Every square matrix \(A\) over an algebraically closed field is similar to a Jordan matrix, unique up to reordering its Jordan blocks.
100: If a family of bounded linear operators on a Banach space is bounded at every vector, then their operator norms are uniformly bounded.
101: For a closed oriented \(n\)-manifold \(M\), cap product with the fundamental class gives \(H^k(M)\cong H_{n-k}(M)\), with the usual coefficient and homology conventions.
102: For every integer \(k\ge 1\), every set of integers with positive upper density contains arithmetic progressions of length \(k\).
103: The number of standard Young tableaux of shape \(\lambda\) is \(f^\lambda=\frac{n!}{\prod_{u\in\lambda}h(u)}\), where \(n=|\lambda|\) and \(h(u)\) is the hook length of cell \(u\).
104: A set of first-order sentences has a model if every finite subset has a model.
105: In a projective plane, if corresponding vertices \(A_i,A_i\prime\) of two triangles lie on concurrent lines, then the three intersections of corresponding sides are collinear, and conversely.
106: For every \(n\ge 1\), the nth cyclotomic polynomial \(\Phi_n(x)\) is irreducible over \(\mathbb{Q}\).
107: The nth Catalan number is \(C_n=\frac{1}{n+1}\binom{2n}{n}\), for \(n\ge 0\).
108: In a triangulation of an \(n\)-simplex with vertices labeled \(0,\ldots,n\), if each boundary vertex uses only labels of its containing face, then some small \(n\)-simplex has all \(n+1\) labels.

110: Every sequence of \((n-1)^2+1\) distinct real numbers contains an increasing subsequence of length \(n\) or a decreasing subsequence of length \(n\).
111: The sum of the reciprocals of the prime numbers diverges.
113: Every continuous real-valued function on a compact interval can be uniformly approximated by polynomials.
114: Every simply connected proper domain in \(\mathbb{C}\) is conformally equivalent to the open unit disk.
115: A locally bounded family of holomorphic functions on a domain is normal: every sequence has a subsequence converging uniformly on compact subsets.
116: Every nonconstant entire function omits at most one complex value.
117: The Radon transform is injective on compactly supported smooth functions: if all hyperplane integrals of \(f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)\) vanish, then \(f=0\).
118: A continuous vector field \(X\) on a path-connected open domain has path-independent line integrals exactly when \(X=\nabla\phi\) for a potential \(\phi\); on a simply connected domain, a continuously differentiable curl-free field is conservative.
119: If the right-hand side \(F(t,y)\) of an ODE is continuous in \(t\) and locally Lipschitz in \(y\), each initial condition \(y(t_0)=y_0\) has a unique local solution.
120: For \(p\ge 1\), the \(L^p\) norm satisfies \(\|f+g\|_p\le\|f\|_p+\|g\|_p\) whenever \(f,g\in L^p\).
121: Every positive linear functional \(L:C(K)\to\mathbb{R}\), for compact Hausdorff \(K\), is integration against a unique finite regular Borel measure \(\mu\) on \(K\): \(L(f)=\int_K f\,d\mu\).
122: A family of probability measures on a Polish space is relatively compact for weak convergence if and only if it is tight.

124: For nonnegative measurable \(f\) on a product measure space, the iterated integrals equal the product integral; for integrable \(f\), the same equality holds and the sections are integrable almost everywhere.

130: For a finite family of convex sets in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), if every \(d+1\) of them intersect, then all of them intersect.
131: Given \(d+2\) points in \(\mathbb{R}^d\), their indices can be partitioned into two nonempty parts whose convex hulls intersect.
132: In every finite-capacity network, the maximum value of a flow equals the capacity of a minimum source–sink cut.
133: For a finite connected graph \(G\), any cofactor of its Laplacian matrix equals the number of spanning trees of \(G\).
134: For a family of finite sets, if every finite subfamily satisfies Hall’s condition, then there is a system of distinct representatives for the whole family.
135: Finite graphs are well-quasi-ordered by the graph-minor relation: every infinite sequence \(G_1,G_2,\ldots\) contains \(i<j\) such that \(G_i\) is a minor of \(G_j\).
136: If \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is open and \(f:U\to\mathbb{R}^n\) is continuous and injective, then \(f(U)\) is open and \(f\) is a homeomorphism onto its image.

138: If there are injections \(A\to B\) and \(B\to A\), then there is a bijection between \(A\) and \(B\).
139: Every sentence that is true in all models of a first-order theory is provable from that theory (for classical first-order logic).
140: Every consistent, effectively axiomatized theory strong enough to represent elementary arithmetic is incomplete: some sentence is neither provable nor refutable in it.
141: In the ring of integers of a number field, every nonzero ideal factors uniquely as a product of prime ideals.
142: Every finite subgroup of the multiplicative group of a field is cyclic.
143: Every simply connected Riemann surface is conformally equivalent to the sphere \(\widehat{\mathbb{C}}\), the complex plane \(\mathbb{C}\), or the open unit disk \(\mathbb{D}\).
144: For an elliptic differential operator on a compact manifold, the analytic index equals the topological index specified by its symbol class.
145: For a smooth projective curve \(C\) of genus \(g\) over \(\mathbb{F}_q\), \(\left|\#C(\mathbb{F}_q)-(q+1)\right|\le 2g\sqrt{q}\).
146: The normalized Jones polynomial is unchanged by ambient isotopy of oriented links.
147: Every Riemannian manifold of constant sectional curvature is locally isometric to the corresponding spherical, Euclidean, or hyperbolic model space.
148: On a compact Riemannian manifold, every de Rham cohomology class has a unique harmonic representative.
149: For every continuous map \(f:S^n\to\mathbb{R}^n\), there is \(x\in S^n\) with \(f(x)=f(-x)\).
150: For a finite-dimensional Lagrangian system with Lagrangian \(\mathcal{L}\), every differentiable continuous symmetry of the action yields a quantity \(Q\) conserved along solutions of the Euler–Lagrange equations: \(\frac{dQ}{dt}=0\).
